newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures paused for breath on Tuesday after gaining more than a point and a half so far this month, awaiting further details on the state of public deficits in France and Germany.
The September contract touched a new contract high of 130.66 early in the session but drifted lower with Bunds to settle down for the first time in six sessions at 130.38.
Steady demand for cash bonds from domestic investors, especially further along the yield curve, ensured 10-year French yields remained some 14 basis points below their German counterparts.

"Today's move was just a reflection of the fact yesterday's move took place on relativley thin volume as there's no real reason to sell," Stuart Thomson, chief market economist at Credit Agricole Indosuez said.
"The U.S. (bond market) will have to lead Europe as Europe is waiting for what the Germans will say (about the 1997 deficit) on Friday," he said.

An analyst at a French brokerage said "the market fell back on profit-taking which suggests it had become overbought." He also said there had been some switching into Bunds late in the session which weighed slightly.

Analysts said there was little hard news from a speech by French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn and it was unlikely the government would unveil its position on the 1997 public deficit until the Germans had set the standard.

"He's really not adding anything new...all we're seeing is the floating of balloons, deliberate leaks to gauge the reaction in markets," Thomson said. "They're not going to make any decisions until they've seen what the Germans will do."
The extra liquidity expected from the maturity of the Balladur bond on July 16 ensured the heady pace of French franc bond issuance seen so far this week continued on Tuesday.

Some 14 billion francs of long-dated domestic bonds and franc eurobonds have already been issued this week attracting fair demand, especially given the fact long-dated government bond yields have fallen close to lows for the year.
"The euro issues have been launched to mop up extra demand from the Balladur bond and as yields are getting to the lows of earlier this year people are getting squeezed in," Thomson said.
September PIBOR remained steady despite some slippage in the franc against the mark. It fell to 3.3733 from 3.3709 late on Monday and close to yesterday's low of 3.3739.
